title: Discord Rich Presence & OAuth
description: Learn how to set custom Discord Rich Presence and authenticate players via Discord OAuth2 on the client in JavaScript and Lua.
codeSnippets:
-- Update presence: (state, details); '' clears a line
    mp.discord.updateRichPresence('Exploring Night City', 'Cruising through Heywood')

    -- Reset presence text (keeps the CyberMP card and timer)
    mp.discord.updateRichPresence('', '')

local DISCORD_APP_ID = '123456789012345678'
    local SCOPES = '["identify", "guilds"]' -- Must be a JSON array string

    local function requestDiscordAuth()
      mp.spawnTask(function()
        while true do
          -- Asynchronous: returns empty string until the user approves
          local code = mp.discord.getCodeAuthorization(DISCORD_APP_ID, SCOPES)

          if code and #code > 0 then
            print("[Discord] Auth code received. Forwarding to server...")

            -- Forward code to the server to exchange for user profile
            mp.events.triggerServer('auth:discordCode', code)
            return
          end
          mp.wait(1000)
        end
      end)
    end

    mp.commands.add('link-discord', requestDiscordAuth)
plainText: The client runtime integrates with the Discord desktop app via the interface. This allows your server to display dynamic status information (such as district, active gig, or faction) on players' Discord profile cards, and securely authenticate player accounts through Discord OAuth2 without asking for login credentials. For full method signatures, see the [](/reference/client/api/global/mpdiscord/) API reference and the Lua Client Reference. --- Rich Presence Rich Presence updates the status text displayed under the player's Discord profile card: #### JS: #### Lua: - and : Optional strings describing the player's current activity. Missing arguments clear the text. - Clearing presence: Calling without arguments in JavaScript (or in Lua) resets the custom status lines while keeping the CyberMP application card and playtime counter visible. :::tip[Rate Limiting] Discord rate-limits Rich Presence updates. Update status when significant events occur (such as switching districts or starting missions), avoiding updates faster than every 15–20 seconds. ::: --- Discord OAuth2 Authentication To verify player identity or link Discord accounts, request a one-time authorization code from the Discord client running on the user's system: #### JS: #### Lua: Authorization Flow Details - (Lua: ): Requests an authorization code. It is asynchronous and non-blocking—it returns an empty string on initial calls and until the user approves the prompt in Discord. - : Must be a JSON-encoded string array (e.g. ), not comma-separated text. - Direct Access Token: If your client needs a direct token from the Discord Game SDK instead of exchanging on the server, you can call . Like the authorization call, it returns an empty string until resolved. - Discord Desktop Required: If Discord is not running on the client machine, these methods continually return . Always guard the polling interval with a timeout. :::caution[Never Expose Client Secrets] Never put your Discord application in client-side code. The client script only retrieves the temporary authorization code; your server backend must perform the token exchange with Discord's REST API. :::

title: Working with Events
description: Learn how to handle local, server, and CEF events on the client side in JavaScript and Lua.
codeSnippets:
-- Platform event: triggers when this client resource completes startup
    mp.events.add('resourceStart', function()
      print('The client resource has successfully started.')
    end)

    -- Platform event: triggers when an entity enters streaming range
    mp.events.add('vehicleStreamIn', function(netID, gameID)
      print(string.format("Vehicle streamed in - NetID: %s, GameID: %s", netID, gameID))
    end)

    -- Custom local event: listening for a local signal
    mp.events.add('myCustomEvent', function(data)
      print('Received local data:', data)
    end)

    -- Emitting a custom local event
    mp.events.trigger('myCustomEvent', { status = 'ok', timestamp = os.time() })

-- Send a reliable packet to the server
    mp.events.triggerServer('requestVehicleSpawn', 'Vehicle.v_sport1_quadra_turbo_r_player')

    -- Listen for events dispatched from the server
    mp.events.addServer('serverNotification', function(message)
      print(string.format("[Server]: %s", message))
    end)

-- Built-in CEF event: fires when the browser DOM is ready
    mp.events.addCef('domReady', function(frameName)
      print(string.format("Browser frame '%s' is ready.", frameName))

      -- Send initial data to the CEF web page
      mp.events.triggerCef('initializeDashboard', { playerName = 'V', health = 100 })
    end)

    -- Built-in CEF event: fires on uncaught JS errors in the browser
    mp.events.addCef('loadingFailed', function(err)
      print(string.format("CEF error in %s: %s", err.frameName, err.message))
    end)

    -- Custom event: dispatched from the CEF page via mp.events.emit
    mp.events.addCef('uiAction', function(actionName, payload)
      print(string.format("User triggered UI action: %s", actionName))
    end)

local function handleVehicleStream(netID, gameID)
      print(string.format("Vehicle %s streamed in.", netID))
    end

    -- Register listener (returns a numeric handler id)

    mp.events.remove('vehicleStreamIn', handlerId)

title: Client Lifecycle & Stages
description: Understand the sequence of resource initialization, game stages, world loading, and safe spawning in JavaScript and Lua.
codeSnippets:
-- 1. Immediate: Register network listeners and console commands
    mp.events.addServer('serverNotification', function(msg)
      print("[Server]: " .. msg)
    end)

    mp.commands.add('ping', function()
      print("Client script active.")
    end)

    -- 2. World Ready: Safe to query player and world systems
    mp.registerGameState('onGameLoaded', function()
      local player = Game.GetPlayer()
      print("World loaded, local player ready:", player ~= nil)

      -- Trigger safe spawn
      mp.client.spawnPlayer(-1392.637, 1271.536, 123.082, 1.0)
    end)

-- mp.wait needs a coroutine: call this from a task or a handler
    local function waitForPlayer(timeoutMs)
      local started = mp.getTimer()
      while mp.getTimer() - started < (timeoutMs or 10000) do
        local player = Game.GetPlayer()
        if player then return player end
        mp.wait(50)
      end
      return nil
    end

    mp.registerGameState('onGameLoaded', function()
      mp.client.spawnPlayer(-1392.637, 1271.536, 123.082, 1.0)

      mp.spawnTask(function()
        local player = waitForPlayer(10000)
        print('Player ready:', player ~= nil)
      end)
    end)

local previewVehicle = nil

    mp.events.add('resourceStop', function()
      -- 1. Despawn client-only preview entities
      if previewVehicle then
        mp.client.despawnVehicle(previewVehicle)
        previewVehicle = nil
      end

      -- 2. Release CEF focus
      mp.cef.setFocus(false, false)
    end)

Attempting to query the player, access world systems, or teleport inside will fail or return . --- Lifecycle Stages Overview --- Stage Reference Stage JavaScript API Lua API Safe to Execute Unsafe to Execute :--- :--- :--- :--- :--- Register events, RPC handlers, commands Any REDengine native calls Read/write TweakDB records and flats Assuming the local player puppet exists Method observers, overrides, early hooks World entity queries / Retrieve , systems, spawn routines Assuming puppet exists synchronously Release CEF focus, clear ticks, despawn local entities Starting new asynchronous work :::note[Post-Load Script Execution] If a client resource starts or restarts when the game is already loaded (such as after a restart or hot reload), queued handlers for and run on the very first script tick. ::: --- Safe Initialization Pattern Keep event and command registration immediate at script root, but defer all world interactions and engine native calls until : #### JS: #### Lua: For complete spawn setup (including health pools), see Spawning the Player. --- Polling for the Player Puppet Calling the spawn method initiates asynchronous entity streaming. The player puppet might not be available on the exact frame the spawn method returns . When applying custom appearances, stat modifications, or inventory items immediately after spawning, poll until returns a valid instance: #### JS: #### Lua: :::caution[Incomplete Puppet State] Immediately after spawn, calling on the puppet can report a placeholder or sentinel value (). Do not apply character-specific meshes or body morphs until the puppet has fully streamed into the world. ::: --- Teardown and Cleanup When a resource stops, its JavaScript context or Lua state is destroyed. However, external states created by your script (such as client-only preview vehicles, active render ticks, or CEF mouse focus) persist unless explicitly cleaned up: #### JS: #### Lua:

Other connected players will not see or interact with them. This is ideal for dealership showcase rooms, cinematic camera sequences, or decorative UI scenes: #### JS: #### Lua: Similar methods exist for pedestrians ( / ) and objects ( / ). Note that local entities in JavaScript reside under [](/reference/client/api/global/mplocal/), whereas in Lua they reside under [](/reference/lua/client/#local-entities-mpclient). --- Per-Frame Tick Loops When implementing custom 3D markers, distance math, or camera updates, execute logic on every render frame: #### JS: #### Lua: :::tip[Performance] Never perform database operations, heavy JSON parsing, or bulk entity queries inside a tick callback. title: Local Storage
description: Learn how to persist client-side preferences and configuration data across game sessions using mp.localStorage in JavaScript and Lua.
codeSnippets:
-- 1. Store primitive string values
    mp.localStorage.set('hud_theme', 'cyberpunk_neon')
    mp.localStorage.set('master_volume', '0.85')

    -- 2. Store structured tables using JSON serialization
    local customKeybinds = {
      openPhone = "T",
      toggleRadio = "R",
      quickHeal = "H"
    }
    mp.localStorage.set('user_keybinds', json.encode(customKeybinds))

    -- 3. Commit changes to physical disk
    mp.localStorage.save()

    -- 4. Retrieve values: get() returns JSON-encoded text ('"abc"', 'null' when missing)
    local rawTheme = mp.localStorage.get('hud_theme')
    local theme = (rawTheme and rawTheme ~= 'null') and json.decode(rawTheme) or nil
    local rawKeybinds = mp.localStorage.get('user_keybinds')
    local keybinds = {}
    if rawKeybinds and rawKeybinds ~= 'null' then
      keybinds = json.decode(json.decode(rawKeybinds)) -- unwrap the store, then parse the value
    end

    print(string.format("Loaded theme: %s, Phone keybind: %s", theme, keybinds.openPhone))

-- Remove a single key
    mp.localStorage.delete('hud_theme')
    mp.localStorage.save()

    -- Clear all stored keys in local storage
    mp.localStorage.deleteAll()
    mp.localStorage.save()
plainText: The client runtime provides persistent key-value storage via . Data saved here is written to the user's local machine and persists across game restarts and server reconnections without requiring server-side database storage. For complete method signatures, see the [](/reference/client/api/global/mplocalstorage/) reference and the Lua Client Reference. --- API Overview The interface exposes five core operations: Method Description :--- :--- Associates a plaintext string value with the specified key in memory. Retrieves the string value associated with the key, or / if not found. Permanently removes a specific key-value entry from storage. Clears all stored key-value entries for this storage database. Flushes in-memory data to physical disk. :::important[Always Call ] Mutations made via , , or are held in memory until is called. If the game client or resource terminates before is executed, pending changes will be lost. Always invoke after writing or removing data. ::: --- Storing and Retrieving Values Values must be plaintext strings. To store structured data (such as objects, arrays, or tables), serialize them with JSON before saving: #### JS: #### Lua: --- Deleting Entries Use to remove a specific configuration entry, or to reset the storage database completely. Remember to call afterwards to commit the deletion: #### JS: #### Lua: --- Storage Scope and Isolation - Client-Side Only: Local storage is completely isolated to the user's machine. It is not automatically transmitted to the server. If the server needs stored client preferences, forward them via server events or RPC. - Per-Server Isolation: Local storage is partitioned per server address (). Resources running on the same server share the storage namespace. To avoid naming collisions between independent resources, prefix your keys with the resource name (e.g. ).

title: Observing Game Methods
description: Learn how to monitor REDengine method calls without altering their execution using observe hooks in JavaScript and Lua.
codeSnippets:
local settingsMenu = nil

    mp.registerGameState('onInit', function()
      -- Observe when the settings menu controller opens
      mp.observe('SettingsMainGameController', 'OnMenuChanged', function(self)
        settingsMenu = self
        print("Settings menu opened.")
      end)

      -- Observe when the settings menu controller requests close
      mp.observe('SettingsMainGameController', 'RequestClose', function(self)
        settingsMenu = nil
        print("Settings menu closed.")
      end)
    end)
plainText: The observe API allows client scripts to listen to internal REDengine methods whenever they are invoked by the game engine. Observers act as passive listeners: they do not modify return values or prevent the underlying game function from executing. For complete type signatures, see [](/reference/client/api/global/observefunction/) and the Lua Client Reference. --- Registering an Observer Register observers from the lifecycle stage. #### JS: #### Lua: --- Method Signatures and Arguments Class and method names correspond directly to definitions found in NativeDB. - Instance Methods: The callback receives . The first argument is the instance of the game object executing the method. - Static Methods: The callback receives without a reference. - No Continuation Function: Observers never receive ; it is appended only to overrides. - Overloaded Signatures: If a method has multiple signatures in NativeDB, supply the full signature suffix (e.g. , ). - No Result Modification: Observers receive (for instance methods) and then the method arguments; they cannot alter return values or cancel function execution. :::warning[Weak References] The reference passed into the callback is a weak pointer into the game engine's memory pool. Never assume a stored controller or entity reference remains valid once the corresponding entity or menu is closed or destroyed. ::: --- Execution Timing & Variants The engine provides several observer variants to control capture timing and thread dispatching: Method Variant Capture Point Dispatch Behavior :--- :--- :--- / Before original method executes Queued onto the script thread (runs on next tick) After original method executes Queued onto the script thread (runs on next tick) / Before original method executes Dispatched immediately without tick queuing After original method executes Dispatched immediately without tick queuing #### JS: #### Lua: :::warning[Raw callbacks run on the game thread] A raw observer runs synchronously inside the hooked game call, often on a job worker thread rather than the script thread, so the resource runtime is not freely available there. Keep raw callbacks to reading the arguments, and forward real work through the queued variants (, , ) or the client deferred queue ( in JS, in Lua). ::: :::tip[Observer vs Override] Observers cannot alter return values or prevent a game function from executing. If you need to intercept, replace, or block a game method, use Method Overrides. :::

title: Overriding Game Methods
description: Learn how to intercept, replace, or chain REDengine method calls using method overrides in JavaScript and Lua.
codeSnippets:
mp.registerGameState('onInit', function()
      -- Force vehicle summoning to always be permitted
      -- Signature suffix specifies overload: IsSummoningVehiclesRestricted;GameInstance
      mp.override(
        'VehicleSystem',
        'IsSummoningVehiclesRestricted;GameInstance',
        function(gameInstance, wrappedMethod)
          return false -- Vehicle summoning is never restricted
        end
      )
    end)
plainText: Unlike passive observers, method overrides ( in Lua / in JS) completely intercept REDengine method invocations. An override function has full control over execution: it can invoke the original method, modify incoming parameters, return a custom result, or prevent the vanilla game method from executing entirely. For complete type signatures, see [](/reference/client/api/global/overridefunction/) and the Lua Client Reference. --- Registering a Method Override Overrides are registered inside the lifecycle stage when game classes become available: #### JS: #### Lua: --- The Continuation Function () The last parameter passed to your override callback is the continuation function . - Chaining Execution: Calling invokes the next registered override in the chain or the vanilla REDengine function. - Do Not Pass : When calling , omit the reference. The runtime bridge already retains the internal instance context. - Blocking Execution: Omitting the call completely cancels the vanilla method logic and skips further execution. - Return Values and Out Parameters: An override may replace the method's result and its values instead of calling the original. A result that is not returned falls back to the type default (Lua) or keeps the current value (JS); an value that is not returned keeps what (or the original call) produced. See Handling Methods with Out Parameters. - Synchronous Execution Only: Overrides run synchronously. Never mark the callback or return a Promise; the game engine expects immediate C++ return values. --- Blocking Game Features (Example) To disable or override specific vanilla gameplay mechanics (such as vehicle summoning restrictions or encumbrance), return custom values directly without invoking : #### JS: #### Lua: --- Handling Methods with Out Parameters For game methods with output parameters ( values in REDscript), return the primary result followed by the out values. The shape of the return value differs between the languages: #### JS: An override returns one array: the return value first, then every value in declaration order. A bare value is also accepted when the method has a single result. - Only a result: return (or ). - Result and one out value: return . - Void method with out values: return . , or an array element that is , keeps the current value; resets the slot to the type default. #### Lua: An override returns multiple values, not a table: the return value first, then every value in declaration order. - Only a result: - Result and one out value: - Void method with out values: A Lua table is treated as one value, not as a list of results: it fails the type conversion and is logged as . A result that is not returned fills the return slot with the type default; an out value that is not returned keeps what returned; returning for an out value resets it to the default.

title: Spawning the Player
description: Learn how to configure player health stat pools and safely spawn the local player in JavaScript and Lua.
codeSnippets: use_game_natives = true

local HEALTH_STAT_POOL_TYPE = 17
    local HEALTH_STAT_TYPE = 787
    local ADDITIVE_MODIFIER_TYPE = 0

    local function setHealth(value)
      local player = Game.GetPlayer()
      local playerGameId = player:GetEntityID()
      local statPoolsSystem = Game.GetStatPoolsSystem()

      statPoolsSystem:RequestSettingStatPoolValueIgnoreChangeMode(
        playerGameId,
        HEALTH_STAT_POOL_TYPE,
        value,
        nil,
        false
      )
    end

    local function setMaxHealth(value)
      local player = Game.GetPlayer()
      local playerGameId = player:GetEntityID()

      local statsSystem = Game.GetStatsSystem()
      statsSystem:RemoveAllModifiers(playerGameId, HEALTH_STAT_TYPE, true)

      local modifier = NewObject('gameConstantStatModifierData_Deprecated')
      modifier.statType = HEALTH_STAT_TYPE
      modifier.modifierType = ADDITIVE_MODIFIER_TYPE
      modifier.value = value
      statsSystem:AddModifier(playerGameId, modifier)

      local statPoolsSystem = Game.GetStatPoolsSystem()
      statPoolsSystem:RequestSettingStatPoolValueIgnoreChangeMode(
        playerGameId,
        HEALTH_STAT_POOL_TYPE,
        value,
        nil,
        true
      )
    end

local SPAWN_HEALTH = 300
    -- Coordinates near V's Megabuilding H10 apartment: [x, y, z, yaw]
    local DEFAULT_SPAWN = {-1392.637, 1271.536, 123.082, 1.0}

    local function spawnPlayer(x, y, z, yaw)
      setMaxHealth(SPAWN_HEALTH)
      setHealth(SPAWN_HEALTH)

      mp.client.spawnPlayer(x, y, z, yaw or 1.0)
    end

-- Spawn automatically when the world is ready
    mp.registerGameState('onGameLoaded', function()
      spawnPlayer(table.unpack(DEFAULT_SPAWN))
    end)

    -- Register a client console command for manual respawn (press F8)
    mp.commands.add('spawn', function()
      spawnPlayer(table.unpack(DEFAULT_SPAWN))
    end)
plainText: In CyberMP, player spawning is coordinated on the client. local pauseMenu = nil

    mp.registerGameState('onInit', function()
      -- Track Settings Menu

      end)

      local targetRotation = EulerAngles.new(0, 0, yaw or 1.0)

        targetPosition,

    end

    end)

plainText: By default, clients download every file listed in a resource's [](/guides/resources/adding-resource-files) array directly from the dedicated server. This includes CEF UI assets, / packs, and tweak files. For servers with many players or large custom assets, this can saturate the server's upload bandwidth and slow down connection times. A resource CDN lets you host those files on an external HTTP server (or a traditional CDN provider) so that clients fetch them from a fast, dedicated download endpoint instead of the game server itself. :::note Resource CDN is available on Server Manager plans starting from Bronze. If the listing plan is below Bronze, the server logs a warning and falls back to serving files through its built-in file server. ::: --- How It Works When CDN is enabled, the dedicated server process separates into two concerns: The server process retains: - configuration and all logic - Entity streaming, events, and RPC - The allow-list (clients still validate downloads against it) The CDN hosts: - The packed client files of every started resource that is not marked as — this includes , and all entries Typical CDN-hosted assets include: Asset type Examples :--- :--- Game archives Vehicle packs, clothing, weapons () REDmod / ArchiveXL extras files, tweak overrides UI assets Images, bundled HTML/CSS/JS for CEF :::tip If you use hot reload during development, keep frequently edited HTML and JS files inside the resource rather than on the CDN. Hot reload watches local resource files — changes pushed to the CDN won't be detected automatically. ::: --- Setting Up CDN Step 1 — Pack the client files Run the server with the flag. This loads , starts all resources, writes the packed client files along with a manifest into a directory, and then exits: You can optionally pass and if your server binds to a non-default address. Step 2 — Upload to your CDN Upload the entire contents of the directory to the root of your CDN domain. The directory structure must be preserved exactly as generated — clients will request files by their relative paths. Step 3 — Configure Add the following keys to your and start the server normally: :::caution These keys are not exposed on the [](/reference/server/api/global/config/serverconfig/) type directly — in they fall under its index signature. Do not attempt to read them as typed properties. ::: --- Re-packing After Changes Every time you add, remove, or update resource files (new archives, updated UI builds, etc.), you need to repeat the pack-and-upload cycle: 1. Stop the server (or run a separate instance with ) 2. Re-run with to regenerate 3. Upload the updated files to your CDN 4. Restart the server --- Core Files The built-in resource includes core files located in that are configured via the setting. These files must be streamed to clients for proper connection. When packaging files for CDN via , ensure these files are packed and uploaded to your CDN. See the section of the server configuration reference for the complete list of required files.

mp.commands.add('ping', function(player, args)

        -- Invoked by a player in the client F8 console

      else

-- Invocation (F8 console): sethealth 500
    mp.commands.add('sethealth', function(player, args)
      -- Reject execution from the server terminal where there is no player entity
      if player == 0 then
        print('[Command] sethealth can only be executed by a player in-game.')
        return
      end

      if not args[1] then
        player:trigger('chat:add', 'Usage: sethealth <amount>')
        return
      end

      local amount = tonumber(args[1])
      if not amount or amount < 0 or amount > 1000 then
        player:trigger('chat:add', 'Error: Health must be between 0 and 1000.')
        return
      end

      player:trigger('player:setHealth', amount)
      player:trigger('chat:add', string.format("Your health was updated to %s HP.", amount))
    end)

-- Invocation (F8 console): veh [model] [appearance]
    mp.commands.add('veh', function(player, args)
      if player == 0 then
        print('[Command] veh can only be executed by a player in-game.')
        return
      end

      local modelName = args[1] or 'Vehicle.v_sport1_quadra_turbo_r_player'
      local appearanceName = args[2] or 'quadra_turbo_r__basic_player_01'

      local modelHash = tonumber(mp.hashes.toTweakdbid(modelName), 10)
      local appearanceHash = tonumber(mp.hashes.toCname(appearanceName), 10)

      local pos = player.position
      local rad = math.rad(player.yaw)
      local spawnX = pos[1] + math.sin(-rad) * 4
      local spawnY = pos[2] + math.cos(-rad) * 4

      local vehicle = mp.vehicles.create({
        model = modelHash,
        appearance = appearanceHash,
        position = vector3(spawnX, spawnY, pos[3]),
        yaw = player.yaw,
        dimension = player.dimension,
      })

      player:trigger('chat:add', string.format("Spawned vehicle #%s (%s).", vehicle.id, modelName))
    end)

-- Invocation (F8 console): tp <x> <y> <z>
    mp.commands.add('tp', function(player, args)
      if player == 0 then
        print('[Command] tp can only be executed by a player in-game.')
        return
      end

      if #args < 3 then
        player:trigger('chat:add', 'Usage: tp <x> <y> <z>')
        return
      end

      local x, y, z = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2]), tonumber(args[3])
      if not x or not y or not z then
        player:trigger('chat:add', 'Error: Invalid coordinates provided.')
        return
      end

      player:trigger('player:teleport', x, y, z)
      player:trigger('chat:add', string.format("Teleported to [%s, %s, %s].", x, y, z))
    end)

    -- Invocation (F8 console): goto <playerId>
    mp.commands.add('goto', function(player, args)
      if player == 0 then
        print('[Command] goto can only be executed by a player in-game.')
        return
      end

      local targetId = tonumber(args[1])
      if not targetId or not mp.players.exists(targetId) then
        player:trigger('chat:add', string.format("Player ID #%s not found.", tostring(args[1])))
        return
      end

      local target = mp.players.at(targetId)
      local pos = target.position

      player.dimension = target.dimension
      player:trigger('player:teleport', pos[1] + 1, pos[2] + 1, pos[3])
      player:trigger('chat:add', string.format("Teleported to %s.", target.nickname))
    end)

-- Invocation: kick <playerId> [reason...]
    mp.commands.add('kick', function(player, args)
      -- If invoked by a player via F8 console, verify admin permissions
      if player ~= 0 and not player:getMeta('isAdmin') then
        player:trigger('chat:add', 'Error: Access denied.')
        return
      end

      local targetId = tonumber(args[1])
      if not targetId or not mp.players.exists(targetId) then
        local errorMsg = string.format("Player ID #%s not found. Usage: kick <playerId> [reason...]", tostring(args[1]))
        if player ~= 0 then
          player:trigger('chat:add', errorMsg)
        else
          print(string.format("[Command] %s", errorMsg))
        end
        return
      end

      local targetPlayer = mp.players.at(targetId)
      local reasonParts = {}
      for i = 2, #args do
        table.insert(reasonParts, args[i])
      end
      local reason = #reasonParts > 0 and table.concat(reasonParts, ' ') or 'Kicked by administrator'
      local senderName = player ~= 0 and player.nickname or 'Server Console'

      -- Broadcast kick notice to all online players
      for _, p in ipairs(mp.players.toArray()) do
        p:trigger('chat:add', string.format("[Kick] %s was kicked by %s (%s)", targetPlayer.nickname, senderName, reason))
      end

      print(string.format("[Kick] %s was kicked by %s (%s)", targetPlayer.nickname, senderName, reason))
      targetPlayer:kick(reason)
    end)

title: Entity Metadata & Synchronization
description: Learn how to store, manage, and synchronize custom state across entities, players, and the global world.
codeSnippets:
-- Set global metadata (synced to all connected clients)
    mp.meta.setGlobal('serverTime', '22:45', true)
    mp.meta.setGlobal('activeWeather', 'Rain', true)

    -- Set server-only internal metadata
    mp.meta.setGlobal('databaseLatency', 14.2, false)

    -- Read global metadata
    local weather = mp.meta.getGlobal('activeWeather')
    print(string.format("Current weather: %s", weather))

mp.events.add('playerConnected', function(playerId)
      local player = mp.players.at(playerId)

      -- Server-only data (not synced to clients)
      player:setMeta('dbId', 1042)
      player:setMeta('isAdmin', true)

      -- Synced data (visible to clients for UI / nametags)
      mp.meta.setPlayer(player, 'faction', 'Moxes', true)
      mp.meta.setPlayer(player, 'reputation', 450, true)
    end)

    -- Reading player metadata
    mp.commands.add('stats', function(player)
      local faction = player:getMeta('faction') or 'None'
      local rep = player:getMeta('reputation') or 0
      player:trigger('chat:add', string.format("Faction: %s | Reputation: %s", faction, rep))
    end)

-- Synced vehicle state
    mp.meta.setEntity(vehicle, 'isLocked', true, true)
    mp.meta.setEntity(vehicle, 'fuel', 85.5, true)

    -- Server-only data
    mp.meta.setEntity(vehicle, 'ownerDbId', 42, false)

    -- Reading back
    if vehicle:getMeta('isLocked') then
      print(string.format("Vehicle #%s is locked.", vehicle.id))
    end
plainText: The metadata system provides a key-value data storage layer. Rather than creating custom network packets and event handlers for every piece of dynamic game state (such as player money, roles, vehicle fuel, or global weather), metadata allows binding arbitrary values that can optionally synchronize across the network. In this guide, you will learn how to use global, player, and entity metadata in JavaScript and Lua. --- How Metadata Works Metadata can be attached to individual entities (players, vehicles, objects) or stored at the global server scope. The Flag When setting metadata, you can provide an optional boolean parameter: - (default): Stores data only on the server. Clients cannot access or read this data. Ideal for sensitive state such as database IDs, admin privileges, or anti-cheat flags. - : Automatically serializes and synchronizes the value to connected clients streaming that entity.
